cards.name: AI and data-centre boom
cards.story: India becomes a hub for cloud and AI computing. Data centres cluster around Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Noida.
cards.today_note: about 15 TWh of generation in 2025 (our estimate)
cards.conversion_note: the driver is already in TWh generated
refs: 13 TWh in 2024 rising to 57 TWh by 2030
40 to 50 TWh more for AI data centres by 2030
cards.why_baseline: Peer countries' history includes some growth in IT and services load, so a small part is already counted.

cards.name: Clean-air push: electric vehicles
cards.story: Pollution leads to curbs on petrol and diesel vehicles and strong support for electric two-wheelers, buses, cars and trucks.
cards.driver: Share of road vehicle-km driven on electricity
cards.today_note: about 1% of road vehicle-km in 2025 (our estimate; sales shares are much higher than fleet shares)
cards.conversion_note: our assumption of generation per percentage point of road vehicle-km at 2047 traffic: about 10.7 TWh at the charger (the order of magnitude of published full-electrification estimates) plus about 15% network losses. Smaller in earlier years because there is less traffic
refs: about 1,070 TWh a year by 2047 if road transport is fully electric
about 295 TWh by 2050 with ambitious policy
cards.why_baseline: None of the countries the baseline learns from electrified road transport while getting richer, so nothing is already counted.

cards.name: Green hydrogen hub
cards.story: India makes hydrogen with electrolysers as a feedstock for fertiliser, refining and steel-making, and for export, as the National Green Hydrogen Mission intends.
cards.conversion_note: 55 kWh per kg: electrolyser efficiency (about 50 kWh/kg) plus compression, an engineering figure
refs: about 257 TWh for 5 Mt in 2030 (51 TWh per Mt)
about 310 TWh for 5 Mt (62 TWh per Mt)
target of 5 Mt a year by 2030
cards.why_baseline: No peer country produced electrolytic hydrogen at scale, so nothing is already counted.
cards.note: Green hydrogen only counts as green if it runs on its own solar and wind, so this wedge is served by dedicated plants, not the grid plan. The supply panel shows the extra land it needs.

cards.name: Hotter summers
cards.story: Heatwaves become longer and more frequent than in the historical record, pushing air-conditioning and fan use beyond what rising incomes alone would bring.
cards.driver: Extra generation for cooling beyond the income trend
cards.today_note: zero by definition: this card is only the extra heat
cards.conversion_note: the driver is already in TWh generated
refs: a stress test; no study isolates warming from income growth
cards.why_baseline: Cooling that comes with higher incomes is already in the baseline; this card is only the extra heat.

cards.name: Manufacturing push
cards.story: Make in India succeeds: factories for electronics, machinery, batteries, textiles and chemicals raise manufacturing's share of the economy. (Hydrogen for steel is counted on the hydrogen card.)
cards.conversion_note: assumed generation per percentage point of GDP at the 2047 economy's size; smaller in earlier years
refs: about 60 TWh of generation per percentage point by 2047
cards.why_baseline: The development ladder learns from China, Korea and others who industrialised, so about half of a push is already counted.

cards.name: Efficiency drive
cards.story: Tighter appliance, building and motor standards mean the same comfort and output need less generation.
refs: names efficiency among the cheapest levers
cards.why_baseline: The baseline already includes normal efficiency gains; this card is savings beyond them.

cards.name: Domestic oil and gas discovery
cards.story: A large offshore find, like Brazil's pre-salt fields, gives India its own oil and cheap gas.
refs: India makes almost no electricity from oil, so a find changes the mix more than the requirement
cards.why_baseline: Not a requirement wedge: it raises GDP growth a little (which the lenses turn into requirement) and makes gas cheaper for the optimiser. The manufacturing card is a structural shift beyond what GDP growth alone brings, so the two do not overlap.
